focus_areas: Built-in shell/file tools and child-process hardening
Local/remote MCP transport, destination gating, and bearer tokens
Skill discovery, invocation, and dynamic capability grants
Rhai/render APIs and in-process resource boundaries
Policy compilation, ambient resolution, attenuation, and planning
Privileged loader, cgroups, spawning, cleanup, and audit transport
eBPF LSM hooks plus filesystem/exec/network matching
Episode/session/concurrency, transcripts, metrics, and audit attribution
Application/REPL/TUI command surfaces and authorization flow

findings.title: Child policies can omit parent deny regions and regain default-allowed reads
findings.description: Filesystem attenuation checks only child rules. A parent deny outside a child prefix can disappear, while unmatched reads are allowed by the kernel matcher.
findings.exploit_scenario: A ceiling denies /home/user/private, but a child retaining only a /workspace read rule derives successfully and can read the omitted private path.
findings.recommendation: Compare effective decisions over inherited policy state, preserving every parent restriction unless the child is demonstrably stricter.
findings.confidence_reason: Filesystem attenuation checks only child grants, allowing omitted parent denies to disappear even though unmatched reads are allowed by enforcement.

findings.title: A child policy can override protected defaults absent from the attenuation ceiling
findings.description: Protected .git, .bee, .ssh, and .aws denies are injected only during compilation. A child-specific grant can pass authoring-level attenuation against a broad parent and later replace the injected deny during planning.
findings.exploit_scenario: A broad HOME write ceiling relies on the injected ~/.ssh deny; a repository child adds a specific ~/.ssh write rule that passes derivation and overrides the protection.
findings.recommendation: Materialize protected defaults into both effective parent and child policies before attenuation, and require an explicit trusted override.
findings.confidence_reason: Protected defaults exist only after compilation, so authoring-level attenuation can approve a child rule that later overrides an injected deny at the same resolved path.

findings.title: UDP sendto bypasses the connect-only egress allowlist
findings.description: The only network LSM program is socket_connect. Unconnected UDP sendto/sendmsg operations never consult NET_ALLOW.
findings.exploit_scenario: A confined process uses sendto on an unconnected UDP socket to transmit data to an arbitrary IP and port.
findings.recommendation: Mediate datagram destinations at socket_sendmsg or a cgroup network hook that covers every outbound packet.
findings.confidence_reason: The loader attaches only socket_connect, file_open, and bprm_check_security, leaving unconnected UDP sendto/sendmsg without any destination-policy hook.

findings.title: Empty network allowlist disables all egress enforcement
findings.description: Planning sets FLAG_NET_ENFORCED only when destinations are nonempty, and socket_connect allows all traffic when the flag is absent.
findings.exploit_scenario: A child that omits network destinations passes attenuation but can connect to any IP and port.
findings.recommendation: Track network-policy activation independently from allowlist cardinality; an active empty list must deny all.
findings.confidence_reason: Planning sets FLAG_NET_ENFORCED only for nonempty rules and socket_connect explicitly allows all traffic when that flag is absent.

findings.title: File-open-only mediation permits metadata mutation and hard-link path aliasing
findings.description: Only file_open is mediated. Link, rename, unlink, mkdir, symlink, and setattr operations are uncovered, and hard links can expose denied inodes under unrestricted paths. Duplicate candidate F-08-07 cited the same file, line, and category.
findings.exploit_scenario: A workload hard-links a protected file into an allowed directory and opens the alias, or renames/unlinks protected control files without triggering file_open.
findings.recommendation: Cover relevant inode operations and bind sensitive objects to stable inode/mount identity rather than pathname alone.
findings.confidence_reason: Only file_open mediates filesystem access, so metadata operations are uncovered and hard-link aliases can change the pathname later evaluated by policy.

findings.title: Empty executable allowlist disables execution enforcement
findings.description: Planning omits EXEC_ALLOW for an empty list, and bprm_check_security interprets a missing entry as unrestricted execution.
findings.exploit_scenario: A no-exec child policy can run any installed binary or newly written payload.
findings.recommendation: Represent exec enforcement separately from allowlist length; an active empty list must install deny-all execution.
findings.confidence_reason: Planning omits EXEC_ALLOW for an empty list and bprm_check_security explicitly interprets the missing key as unrestricted execution.

findings.title: Attacker-triggerable path-resolution failure fails open
findings.description: File and exec hooks return allow when bpf_d_path fails. The fixed 4096-byte buffer can be exceeded by workload-created deep paths.
findings.exploit_scenario: A process creates a resolved path longer than 4096 bytes and invokes a disallowed relative executable from it, causing path resolution to fail open.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed on path-helper errors for managed scopes and emit an explicit path-unavailable audit event.
findings.confidence_reason: Both file and exec hooks explicitly allow when bpf_d_path fails, and resolved paths can exceed the fixed buffer.

findings.title: Zero-capability filesystem policy defaults to broad read/write access
findings.description: Unmatched reads are always allowed, and unmatched writes are denied only when a flag derived from a positive write grant is set. An empty policy therefore permits broad host access outside injected protected paths.
findings.exploit_scenario: A nominally zero-capability workload reads project secrets or overwrites launcher-user-writable files not covered by an explicit deny.
findings.recommendation: Encode read and write default-deny state explicitly and deny unmatched access in every enforcing scope.
findings.confidence_reason: Missing filesystem state and unmatched paths are explicitly allowed despite the stated deny-by-default authority model.

findings.title: Kernel subtree matcher mishandles root and trailing-slash rules
findings.description: The shared matcher normalizes trailing slashes and special-cases root, but the eBPF mirror does neither. A / rule matches only root, and /secret/ misses descendants.
findings.exploit_scenario: An operator denies / or /home/user/.ssh/, but descendant opens fall through to permissive unmatched behavior.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize encoded patterns and make kernel matching exactly mirror the shared matcher, with conformance tests.
findings.confidence_reason: The eBPF matcher neither normalizes trailing slashes nor special-cases root, contradicting the shared matcher.

findings.title: Tool children retain launcher privileges and can execute privileged descendants
findings.description: Pre-exec hardening only changes dump settings. It does not drop identity or capabilities or set no_new_privs, while privileged-target checks cover only the initial executable.
findings.exploit_scenario: A root-launched shell retains root, or an ordinary checked shell later executes a setuid or file-capability binary.
findings.recommendation: Run tools as a dedicated unprivileged identity, clear all capability sets and groups, and set PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS.
findings.confidence_reason: Child hardening sets only dump controls, never drops identity/capabilities or sets no_new_privs, so an initial shell check cannot prevent later privileged exec.

findings.title: Background descendants survive teardown and become unrestricted
findings.description: Scope teardown only removes the cgroup directory. A surviving descendant makes removal fail, callers ignore the error, and dropping Engine detaches enforcement.
findings.exploit_scenario: A shell backgrounds a redirected process and exits; session teardown fails silently, then the survivor continues after LSM detachment.
findings.recommendation: Use cgroup.kill, wait for populated=0, treat cleanup failure as fatal, and retain enforcement until every descendant is gone.
findings.confidence_reason: A surviving background descendant makes remove_dir fail, the error is ignored, and dropping the engine detaches enforcement while the process remains alive.

findings.title: An empty child network list disables the parent egress allowlist
findings.description: Attenuation accepts an empty child list, while planning clears network enforcement when that list is empty.
findings.exploit_scenario: A child under a crates.io-only ceiling omits network.allow and gains unrestricted egress.
findings.recommendation: Carry parent enforcement activation through derivation and encode an active deny-all empty list.
findings.confidence_reason: Empty child network lists pass attenuation and produce no network-enforced flag, causing unrestricted destinations.

findings.title: Removing the final child write grant disables default-deny writes
findings.description: An empty child filesystem map passes derivation and clears FLAG_FS_WRITE_DEFAULT_DENY because the flag is tied to positive write grants.
findings.exploit_scenario: A child beneath a /workspace-only write ceiling requests no filesystem entries and gains writes to other same-user host paths.
findings.recommendation: Represent unmatched write behavior explicitly and preserve the parent's deny state even when the child has no positive grants.
findings.confidence_reason: An empty child filesystem request passes attenuation and clears the write-default-deny flag, allowing unmatched writes.

findings.title: An empty child executable list turns a restricted parent into unrestricted execution
findings.description: Attenuation validates only child-listed executables. An empty list passes, then planning omits the exec map that would activate enforcement.
findings.exploit_scenario: A child beneath a cargo-and-rustc ceiling omits exec.allow and can run bash, curl, or any other accessible binary.
findings.recommendation: Preserve active exec policy through attenuation and install deny-all when the derived allowlist is empty.
findings.confidence_reason: Empty child exec lists pass the subset loop, produce no executable map, and turn the parent allowlist into unrestricted execution.

findings.title: Privileged children can migrate outside the exact cgroup policy key
findings.description: Children retain UID, groups, and capabilities after joining the scope. Enforcement keys only the exact cgroup ID and fails open for an unregistered descendant or destination cgroup.
findings.exploit_scenario: A root or delegated child creates or joins another cgroup and performs operations under an absent map key.
findings.recommendation: Drop identity and capabilities, set no_new_privs, prevent migration, and enforce by managed ancestry rather than one exact leaf ID.
findings.confidence_reason: Scoped children retain cgroup-management authority while enforcement keys only the exact cgroup ID and fails open elsewhere.

findings.title: Untrusted project config becomes an unbounded execution policy without a user ceiling
findings.description: Repository-local .bee/config.toml may select a project policy. When no trusted ceiling exists, resolution accepts it verbatim as the sandbox and grant base. Duplicate candidate F-06-07 cited the same file, line, and category.
findings.exploit_scenario: A trojan repository selects a policy granting HOME writes, broad execution, and egress; a user with only provider configuration launches bee and silently receives that authority.
findings.recommendation: Reject project-origin policies without a trusted operator ceiling, or treat the absent ceiling as deny-all and require explicit approval.
findings.confidence_reason: Auto-loaded untrusted project policy becomes the effective authority verbatim when no protected ceiling exists.

findings.title: Discovered skill directories are made readable after attenuation
findings.description: Session and episode setup add read grants for every discovered skill directory after ceiling derivation and consent; the episode path also expands its dynamic ceiling.
findings.exploit_scenario: A discovered user skill under a ceiling-denied HOME subtree makes its directory readable to model-controlled file tools.
findings.recommendation: Treat skill resource reads as ordinary requested capabilities and prove them against the protected ceiling before registration.
findings.confidence_reason: Skill-directory read grants are inserted after attenuation and consent, and the episode path expands the dynamic ceiling to bless the unchecked mutation.

findings.title: Provider TOML can send an arbitrary environment secret to an attacker endpoint
findings.description: Repository provider configuration selects both api_key_env and an OpenAI-compatible base_url; batch reads that host variable and supplies it as authentication to the selected endpoint.
findings.exploit_scenario: A provider file names GITHUB_TOKEN and https://attacker.example/v1, causing the first model request to disclose the token.
findings.recommendation: Bind operator-owned credential slots to approved provider origins and require approval for new endpoint/credential pairings.
findings.confidence_reason: Repository provider config selects both a host secret name and destination, and the resolved secret is supplied as authentication to that endpoint.

findings.title: Scenario workdir setup performs host writes before sandbox creation
findings.description: Scenario-controlled create_dirs, create_files, and flag paths reach create_dir_all and std::fs::write before sandbox construction, without rejecting absolute paths, parent traversal, or symlink escapes.
findings.exploit_scenario: A checked-in scenario overwrites an SSH configuration, shell file, or Git hook using an absolute or traversing path.
findings.recommendation: Restrict materialization beneath an operator-created directory and use descriptor-relative no-follow operations.
findings.confidence_reason: Scenario-controlled absolute, parent-traversal, or symlink paths reach privileged host create/write operations before sandbox construction.

findings.title: Repository-controlled workdir paths permit arbitrary host overwrite before sandboxing
findings.description: run_episode materializes uncontained repository scenario paths before creating the enforced scope.
findings.exploit_scenario: A malicious scenario writes ../../.git/hooks/pre-commit or an absolute launcher-user file before any policy applies.
findings.recommendation: Validate relative components, reject symlinks, and perform all materialization through a bounded directory capability.
findings.confidence_reason: Scenario workdir paths receive no containment validation and are passed directly to host-side writes before sandboxing.

findings.title: Tool grants bypass the attenuation ceiling and scenario tool allowlist
findings.description: The ceiling proof covers only filesystem policy. Requested tools are copied into the outcome and registered afterward, so a tool-only request cannot widen the checked candidate.
findings.exploit_scenario: A repository skill requests bash while the scenario exposes only a narrow non-shell tool; automatic consent registers bash anyway.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a protected tool ceiling and require every requested tool to be contained and explicitly approved.
findings.confidence_reason: The ceiling proof covers only filesystem policy while requested tools are subsequently registered.

findings.title: Background descendants survive tool deadlines and outlive enforcement
findings.description: kill_on_drop and wait_with_output cover only the direct shell. Redirected background descendants keep the cgroup nonempty; teardown failure is ignored before Engine detachment.
findings.exploit_scenario: A model backgrounds a process with redirected descriptors, lets the shell exit, and continues after session teardown without bee enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Kill and reap the entire process group and cgroup, verify emptiness, and keep LSM links attached until cleanup succeeds.
findings.confidence_reason: Direct-child lifecycle handling does not cover redirected descendants, and ignored teardown failure precedes enforcement detachment.

findings.title: Scenario ID escapes the batch transcript output directory
findings.description: Scenario validation requires only a nonempty ID. Batch output interpolates that ID into a filename and joins it to the output directory, allowing absolute and parent components. Duplicate candidate F-09-03 cited the same file, line, and category.
findings.exploit_scenario: A scenario ID such as ../../outside/report writes transcript JSON outside --out.
findings.recommendation: Encode the entire identifier as one safe filename component and create the destination relative to an opened output-directory descriptor.
findings.confidence_reason: Unvalidated scenario_id reaches Path::join and std::fs::write, so absolute or parent components escape the selected transcript directory.

findings.title: Repository-controlled scenario IDs escape batch output containment
findings.description: The joined transcript path contains the unsanitized scenario ID, and validation rejects neither absolute paths nor parent components.
findings.exploit_scenario: A repository scenario with id ../../outside/report causes an operator batch run to overwrite a matching file outside results.
findings.recommendation: Use a strict slug or stable hash and verify the destination remains directly beneath the output directory.
findings.confidence_reason: scenario.id reaches transcript filename join/write unchanged and validation rejects neither absolute paths nor parent components.

findings.title: A child can remove an executable inode-pin requirement
findings.description: Attenuation strips the leading inode-pin marker from parent and child before comparison, so an unpinned child path passes a pinned ceiling.
findings.exploit_scenario: A repository removes ! from an allowed mutable tool path, then replaces that path and executes attacker-controlled code.
findings.recommendation: Include pin strength in the attenuation order; a child may add but never remove stable-identity requirements.
findings.confidence_reason: Attenuation explicitly strips the inode-pin marker on both sides, so an unpinned child rule passes a pinned ceiling.

findings.title: Exact cgroup-ID lookup lets migrated processes leave enforcement
findings.description: Every hook permits access when the current exact cgroup ID is absent. Privileged children retain authority to migrate to an unregistered cgroup.
findings.exploit_scenario: A root or delegated workload moves itself to an ancestor or sibling cgroup, then performs denied file, exec, and network operations.
findings.recommendation: Prevent migration, drop child privilege, and use ancestry-aware membership or register all managed descendants.
findings.confidence_reason: Every hook allows on an absent exact cgroup-ID key, while privileged children retain authority to migrate.

findings.title: Unix-domain sockets bypass the network policy
findings.description: socket_connect handles only IPv4 and IPv6 and explicitly allows other families; inherited socket paths can expose local credential and control services.
findings.exploit_scenario: A model-controlled process uses SSH_AUTH_SOCK or an accessible container-runtime socket despite an IP destination allowlist.
findings.recommendation: Deny unsupported families by default and add an explicit AF_UNIX path policy.
findings.confidence_reason: socket_connect explicitly allows non-IP families, so an accessible AF_UNIX service bypasses NET_ALLOW.

findings.title: Privileged-target refusal checks only the first executable
findings.description: Setuid, setgid, and file-capability checks apply only to the initially resolved program and occur before eventual exec; no_new_privs is absent.
findings.exploit_scenario: An allowed shell runs a privileged image later, or an attacker races replacement of the checked pathname.
findings.recommendation: Set no_new_privs, drop credentials, and enforce privileged-image restrictions on every exec transition using stable descriptors.
findings.confidence_reason: Only the initially resolved executable is checked, so a shell/interpreter or path race can later execute a privileged image.

findings.title: Headless episodes grant every discovered skill before invocation
findings.description: run_episode resolves every discovered requires block before invocation, using AllowWithinCeiling as unconditional consent.
findings.exploit_scenario: An unused repository skill requests a sensitive within-ceiling write grant that becomes active for the whole unattended episode.
findings.recommendation: Resolve grants only for explicitly selected or invoked skills, and deny unattended repository requests absent a trusted manifest.
findings.confidence_reason: Headless runs process every discovered requires block with unconditional consent, contradicting the repository-origin HITL model.

findings.title: Credential stripping denylist exposes ambient secrets to model tools
findings.description: Tool commands inherit the complete host environment except a small list of provider variables. Other cloud, GitHub, Kubernetes, and agent credentials remain visible.
findings.exploit_scenario: A prompt-injected shell prints AWS or GitHub variables, and bee returns the output to the external model provider.
findings.recommendation: Use env_clear and rebuild a minimal approved environment, including removal of credential-file and socket handles.
findings.confidence_reason: Child commands inherit the host environment except a small name denylist, giving model-controlled shell code access to other ambient credentials.

findings.title: Unselected repository skills inject instructions into every tool schema
findings.description: Auto-discovered project skill names and descriptions enter the model-visible skill schema verbatim before invocation, and project skills can shadow user skills.
findings.exploit_scenario: A trojan repository supplies a familiar-looking skill whose description directs the model to access credentials or invoke tools.
findings.recommendation: Require operator trust before exposing project skills, prevent silent shadowing, and quote metadata as untrusted data.
findings.confidence_reason: Project skill metadata is auto-discovered, shadows user skills, and enters every model request verbatim before explicit invocation.

findings.title: A child can disable the parent exfiltration controls
findings.description: derive performs no exfiltration comparison, so a child can disable detection and remove sensitive paths.
findings.exploit_scenario: A protected ceiling enables exfiltration detection, but a repository child clears it and avoids the planner refusal that the parent would trigger.
findings.recommendation: Make exfiltration state monotonic: enabled cannot become false and parent-sensitive regions must remain covered.
findings.confidence_reason: Derivation performs no exfiltration comparison, allowing a child to disable or remove ceiling controls.

findings.title: Unknown policy fields are silently ignored
findings.description: Security policy structures do not deny unknown fields. Misspelled restrictive sections disappear silently, and empty exec/network state disables enforcement.
findings.exploit_scenario: A reviewed-looking policy uses a misspelled network or executable section and compiles with that capability unrestricted.
findings.recommendation: Apply serde deny_unknown_fields to the document and all nested security structures.
findings.confidence_reason: Security policy structs do not reject unknown fields, so misspelled sections are ignored and default-empty capability lists disable enforcement.

findings.title: Network-enforced scopes allow every non-IP socket family
findings.description: The family switch returns allow for all non-IPv4/IPv6 sockets, leaving AF_UNIX host services outside the policy.
findings.exploit_scenario: A confined process connects to a local agent, database, or container-control socket without a matching destination grant.
findings.recommendation: Deny unsupported families and introduce family-specific grants, including Unix-socket path authorization.
findings.confidence_reason: The family switch explicitly allows non-IP sockets, making AF_UNIX host-service access a concrete bypass when a useful socket is reachable.

findings.title: Failed scope reload can retain kernel grants after userspace rollback
findings.description: reload_scope mutates maps sequentially. A later fallible network update returns without restoring earlier filesystem or exec changes, while callers roll back only userspace lease state.
findings.exploit_scenario: A map-capacity failure occurs after a filesystem grant is installed; bee reports refusal but the kernel keeps the widened access.
findings.recommendation: Stage changes behind a generation switch or snapshot and fully roll back every successful mutation on error.
findings.confidence_reason: Map mutations occur before fallible network updates with no rollback, leaving kernel authority widened after callers report refusal.

findings.title: Fixed-delay audit draining can lose or misattribute records
findings.description: Concurrent settle is a fixed five-millisecond sleep followed by a nonblocking drain, with no delivery barrier or sequence watermark.
findings.exploit_scenario: A delayed background denial arrives during the next call or after the final drain, corrupting escalation decisions and scoring.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit audit-delivery barrier and final synchronized drain with call or attempt identity.
findings.confidence_reason: The concurrent audit path has no watermark ensuring all events for the completed call arrived.

findings.title: Reactive retry removes the triggering denial from call evidence
findings.description: After a grant and retry, call.audit is replaced with retry-only records even though the original denial remains in the episode trail. Scoring derives coverage from the truncated call field.
findings.exploit_scenario: A denied operation is auto-granted and retried successfully; derived enforcement evidence presents the call as having no denial.
findings.recommendation: Represent attempts separately or retain both initial and retry records, and derive metrics from complete correlated evidence.
findings.confidence_reason: A successful reactive retry overwrites call-level audit, while scoring derives denial coverage and techniques from that field.

findings.title: Hand-written URL parsing can authorize a different host than the transport
findings.description: The domain gate manually parses authorities and disagrees with standards-based HTTP parsing on backslashes and userinfo.
findings.exploit_scenario: A crafted HTTPS URL is gated as allowed.example while the HTTP client connects to evil.example and attaches the configured bearer token.
findings.recommendation: Parse once with the transport's URL type, require HTTPS, and reject userinfo and ambiguous backslashes.
findings.confidence_reason: The hand-written parser treats backslashes differently from standards-based URL parsing, enabling host-policy differentials.

findings.title: Post-hoc nesting validation permits recursive clone amplification
findings.description: layout.add clones arbitrary existing subtrees before checking nesting. A shallow Rhai loop can construct deep Rust graphs and trigger repeated recursive cloning before final validation.
findings.exploit_scenario: A script repeatedly wraps the prior widget, causing quadratic native work or stack exhaustion before the depth-four commit error.
findings.recommendation: Enforce depth incrementally before cloning, track bounded builder metadata, and move rather than deep-clone where possible.
findings.confidence_reason: layout.add clones an existing subtree before nesting validation, enabling large intermediate growth before final commit checks.

findings.title: Model and sandbox output is interpreted as terminal control sequences
findings.description: Provider and tool text reaches the host terminal printer without control-sequence filtering.
findings.exploit_scenario: A tool emits OSC-52 to replace the operator clipboard or CSI sequences to repaint the screen and forge prompts.
findings.recommendation: Escape all untrusted control characters and keep application-generated ANSI separate from external content.
findings.confidence_reason: Model and tool content reaches the host terminal unsanitized, making OSC/CSI/DCS injection clear.

findings.title: Unbounded animation cycles trigger attacker-sized playback allocation
findings.description: Rhai can set cycles up to u32::MAX, and playback eagerly allocates and fills a vector proportional to frame count times cycles.
findings.exploit_scenario: A one-frame animation with billions of cycles requests tens of gigabytes inside the trusted process.
findings.recommendation: Bound cycles, use checked multiplication, and make repeated playback lazy.
findings.confidence_reason: Rhai can set cycles to u32::MAX, after which playback eagerly reserves and fills a proportional vector.

findings.title: Concurrent audit records share one synthetic scope ID
findings.description: The concurrent runner creates one stream labeled bee-concurrent, and cgroup-based demultiplexing never rewrites each event to the real episode scope.
findings.exploit_scenario: A downstream consumer grouping by scope_id collapses distinct episodes and cannot reliably attribute evidence.
findings.recommendation: Stamp the actual subscribed scope after demultiplexing and persist the cgroup-to-scope mapping.
findings.confidence_reason: The shared stream stamps every event with a literal scope ID and demultiplexing never corrects that metadata.

findings.title: Relative filesystem restrictions cannot match resolved kernel paths
findings.description: Unrecognized relative patterns remain relative and compile into prefix rules, while enforcement compares absolute bpf_d_path output.
findings.exploit_scenario: A policy deny for secrets looks restrictive but never matches /work/repo/secrets/key.
findings.recommendation: Reject relative rules or resolve them against an explicit trusted base before attenuation and compilation.
findings.confidence_reason: Relative literal paths are accepted unchanged while enforcement compares resolved absolute paths.

findings.title: Scope teardown leaves cgroup-keyed authorization entries behind
findings.description: Teardown removes only the cgroup directory and leaves SCOPES, filesystem, exec, and network map entries.
findings.exploit_scenario: A reused cgroup inode ID for a stricter scope inherits stale network destinations from an older permissive scope.
findings.recommendation: Delete every tracked per-cgroup key transactionally before removing the directory and reject stale IDs at creation.
findings.confidence_reason: Teardown never deletes authorization maps, so inode-ID reuse can expose stale network grants, though practical reuse needs runtime confirmation.

findings.title: Cgroup ID reuse can combine new scopes with stale map state
findings.description: Directory removal does not clear per-scope maps, and new scope creation does not comprehensively remove network keys for a reused ID.
findings.exploit_scenario: After inode reuse, a restricted scope retains destinations granted only to the prior scope.
findings.recommendation: Track and delete all installed keys before teardown and validate that a new ID has no stale state.
findings.confidence_reason: Teardown removes no per-cgroup map entries, so cgroup-ID reuse can combine new metadata with stale network keys.

findings.title: Terminal control characters in skill metadata can forge consent displays
findings.description: Repository-controlled skill names, tool names, and filesystem paths are printed directly in the y/N capability prompt without control-character escaping.
findings.exploit_scenario: ANSI cursor or clear-screen sequences hide a dangerous within-ceiling request immediately before the operator approves it.
findings.recommendation: Reject or visibly escape control characters and bind approval to a canonical request digest.
findings.confidence_reason: Repository-controlled control characters are printed verbatim inside the authorization prompt, enabling terminal display forgery.

findings.title: Unescaped project skill metadata can forge the capability prompt
findings.description: The authorization UI renders untrusted YAML fields raw before accepting y or yes, allowing ANSI, newline, and bidi display manipulation.
findings.exploit_scenario: A malicious skill redraws a dangerous tool or write grant as benign; an operator approves the forged display.
findings.recommendation: Render a structured, control-safe canonical request and confirm a trusted identifier rather than raw metadata.
findings.confidence_reason: Untrusted skill metadata is rendered raw in a security decision prompt, although exploitation still requires operator approval.

findings.title: Default progress logs expose tool arguments, results, and CTF flags
findings.description: Progress output writes raw prefixes of tool arguments and results to stderr without schema-aware redaction.
findings.exploit_scenario: submit_flag values or credentials at the start of file/tool output enter CI logs and terminal recordings.
findings.recommendation: Log only tool names and metadata by default and redact secret-bearing fields and raw content.
findings.confidence_reason: Default progress output prints raw argument and result prefixes, concretely exposing submitted flags or leading secret content.

findings.title: Remote MCP redirects bypass the destination allowlist
findings.description: The configured URL is checked once, then passed to an HTTP transport without a per-hop destination validation policy.
findings.exploit_scenario: An allowed MCP server redirects a request to loopback, cloud metadata, or a denylisted internal service.
findings.recommendation: Disable redirects or validate every Location target, reject downgrades, and prevent cross-origin credential forwarding.
findings.confidence_reason: The code gates only the initial URL and supplies no redirect policy or per-hop validation.

findings.title: Lazy skill-body reads can be redirected to arbitrary host files
findings.description: Discovery follows links and stores a mutable SKILL.md path. Invocation reopens it host-side without canonical-root containment, stable identity, or sandbox enforcement.
findings.exploit_scenario: A writable skill is replaced with a symlink to an SSH key between discovery and invocation, and the body is returned to the model.
findings.recommendation: Reject symlinks, verify canonical containment, bind to stable file identity, and revalidate frontmatter on invocation.
findings.confidence_reason: The symlink/TOCTOU host-read path is credible, though exploitation needs a suitable writable skill path or race.

findings.title: Repeated panel commits clone large widgets without an aggregate limit
findings.description: Each render_to deep-clones and retains another owned spec. Per-widget and evaluator-operation limits do not enforce a total output-memory budget.
findings.exploit_scenario: A script repeatedly commits a maximum-size chart to one panel, retaining many redundant copies and exhausting process memory.
findings.recommendation: Cap commits, coalesce same-panel updates, and enforce an aggregate byte and element budget.
findings.confidence_reason: Every panel commit retains another owned spec, though existing evaluator limits make the exact memory threshold workload-dependent.

findings.title: Concurrent audit events receive a shared synthetic scope identifier
findings.description: Decoded concurrent records receive the stream-wide bee-concurrent label, while numeric cgroup routing still delivers them to the correct episode.
findings.exploit_scenario: Consumers relying only on the human-readable scope label can confuse records from distinct episodes.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the scope label from the demultiplexer subscription and persist both true scope and cgroup ID.
findings.confidence_reason: The label is inaccurate, but cgroup-based demultiplexing still associates events with the correct episode, leaving low-impact metadata corruption.

findings.title: Stdio MCP servers run with host-user authority in non-enforce builds
findings.description: The mcp feature can be built without enforce, in which case configured stdio servers launch through Sandbox::host with no filesystem or network confinement.
findings.exploit_scenario: A compromised explicitly configured MCP package reads same-user files or reaches the network in documented host mode.
findings.recommendation: Refuse host-mode stdio MCP unless the operator supplies a distinct unsafe opt-in, and surface containment mode before spawn.
findings.confidence_reason: Host mode is explicitly operator-selected and documented as unenforced, so this is likely expected unsafe-mode behavior rather than a vulnerability.
